(p-٥٧٥٧)بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ

سُورَةُ المُمْتَحَنَةِ

(Surat al-Mumtahanah)

بِفَتْحِ الحاءِ، وقَدْ تُكْسَرُ، فَعَلى الأوَّلِ هي صِفَةُ المَرْأةِ الَّتِي نَزَلَتْ فِيها. وعَلى الثّانِي صِفَةُ السُّورَةِ، كَما قِيلَ لِبَراءَةَ (الفاضِحَةُ) كَما في (الأعْلامِ).

Written with a fatha on the ḥā' (al-Mumtaḥanah), it describes the woman concerning whom the surah was revealed. Written with a kasra (al-Mumtaḥinah), it describes the surah itself, just as Bara'ah (Surat al-Tawbah) is called (al-Fāḍiḥah), as stated in (al-A'lam).

قالَ المَهايِمِيُّ: سُمِّيَتْ بِها لِدَلالَةِ آيَةِ الِامْتِحانِ عَلى أنَّهُ لا يُكْتَفى في بابِ الصِّحَّةِ بِظَواهِرِ الأدِلَّةِ كالهِجْرَةِ، بَلْ لا بُدَّ مِنَ اخْتِبارِ البَواطِنِ. فَدَلائِلُ الِاعْتِقاداتِ أوْلى بِذَلِكَ. وهَذا مِن أعْظَمِ مَقاصِدِ القُرْآنِ. انْتَهى.

Al-Mahayimi said: It was named after this because the verse of testing (imtihan) indicates that, in matters of soundness of belief, one does not rely merely on the outward evidences, such as emigration, but the inner states must be tested. The evidences for beliefs are more deserving of this. And this is among the greatest objectives of the Qur'an. End of quotation.

وفِي (جَمالِ القُرّاءِ) أنَّها تُسَمّى سُورَةَ الِامْتِحانِ، وسُورَةَ المَوَدَّةِ. وهي مَدَنِيَّةٌ.

In (Jamal al-Qurra') it is stated that it is called Surat al-Imtihan (the Surah of Testing) and Surat al-Mawaddah (the Surah of Affection). It is a Medinan surah.

وآيُها ثَلاثَ عَشْرَةَ.

Its verses number thirteen.

(p-٥٧٥٨)بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ

القَوْلُ في تَأْوِيلِ قَوْلِهِ تَعالى:

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[١] ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا عَدُوِّي وعَدُوَّكم أوْلِياءَ تُلْقُونَ إلَيْهِمْ بِالمَوَدَّةِ وقَدْ كَفَرُوا بِما جاءَكم مِنَ الحَقِّ يُخْرِجُونَ الرَّسُولَ وإيّاكم أنْ تُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ رَبِّكم إنْ كُنْتُمْ خَرَجْتُمْ جِهادًا في سَبِيلِي وابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاتِي تُسِرُّونَ إلَيْهِمْ بِالمَوَدَّةِ وأنا أعْلَمُ بِما أخْفَيْتُمْ وما أعْلَنْتُمْ ومَن يَفْعَلْهُ مِنكم فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ﴾

﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, extending to them affection, while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, expelling the Messenger and yourselves [merely] because you believe in Allah, your Lord. If you have come out in jihad in My cause and seeking My approval, [then do not] confide to them affection, for I am most knowing of what you conceal and what you declare. And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the sound way.﴾

﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا عَدُوِّي وعَدُوَّكم أوْلِياءَ﴾ أيْ: أنْصارًا. نَهْيٌ لِأصْحابِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَواتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ، عَنْ مُوالاةِ مُشْرِكِي مَكَّةَ المُحارِبِينَ لِلَّهِ ولِرَسُولِهِ وقْتَئِذٍ، لِما فِيها مِنَ الفِتْنَةِ بِالدِّينِ وأهْلِهِ كَما يَأْتِي.

﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as awliya'﴾, meaning: as supporters (anṣar). This is a prohibition addressed to the Companions of the Prophet, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, against allying with the polytheists of Makkah, who were at that time waging war against Allah and His Messenger, because of the trial (fitnah) in religion and its people that it entails, as will come.

﴿تُلْقُونَ إلَيْهِمْ بِالمَوَدَّةِ﴾ أيْ: صَمِيمِ المَحَبَّةِ، والباءُ زائِدَةٌ في المَفْعُولِ ﴿وقَدْ كَفَرُوا بِما جاءَكم مِنَ الحَقِّ﴾ أيْ: مِنَ الإيمانِ بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ وكِتابِهِ، الَّذِي هو نِهايَةُ الهُدى، وغايَةُ السَّعادَةِ.

﴿Extending to them affection﴾, meaning: the pure essence of love. The particle bi- (in bi-l-mawaddah) is redundant (zā'idah) with respect to the object. ﴿While they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth﴾, meaning: of the faith in Allah, His Messenger and His Book, which is the ultimate guidance and the goal of happiness.

ثُمَّ أشارَ إلى أنَّهم لَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ ذَلِكَ حَتّى آذَوُا المُؤْمِنِينَ، بِما يَقْطَعُ العَلائِقَ مَعَهم رَأْسًا، بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿يُخْرِجُونَ الرَّسُولَ وإيّاكُمْ﴾ أيْ: مِن أرْضِكم ودِيارِكم ﴿أنْ تُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ أيْ: يُخْرِجُونَكم لِإيمانِكم بِاللَّهِ، الجامِعِ لِلْكَمالاتِ المُقْتَضِيَةِ انْقِيادَ النّاقِصِ لَهُ، لاسِيَّما بِاعْتِبارِ اتِّصافِهِ بِوَصْفِ كَوْنِهِ رَبّاكم بِالكَمالاتِ، فَهي بِالحَقِيقَةِ عَداوَةٌ مَعَ اللَّهِ.

Then he indicated that this was not enough for them, until they harmed the believers in a manner that severs all ties with them altogether, by His saying: ﴿expelling the Messenger and yourselves﴾, meaning: from your land and your homes. ﴿[merely] because you believe in Allah, your Lord﴾, meaning: they expel you because of your belief in Allah, who combines all the perfections that require the submission of the deficient to Him, particularly in view of His attribute of being your Lord who perfects you. Thus, in reality, this is enmity against Allah.

قالَ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ: هَذا مَعَ ما قَبْلَهُ مِنَ التَّهْيِيجِ عَلى عَداوَتِهِمْ، وعَدَمِ مُوالاتِهِمْ؛ لِأنَّهم أخْرَجُوا الرَّسُولَ وأصْحابَهُ مِن بَيْنِ أظْهُرِهِمْ، كَراهَةً لِما هم عَلَيْهِ مِنَ التَّوْحِيدِ، وإخْلاصِ العِبادَةِ لِلَّهِ وحْدَهُ؛ ولِهَذا قالَ تَعالى:

Ibn Kathir said: This, together with what precedes it, is an incitement to enmity toward them and to not allying with them, because they expelled the Messenger and his Companions from among their midst, out of aversion to what they held of monotheism and sincerity of worship to Allah alone. For this reason, the Exalted said:

﴿أنْ تُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ أيْ: لَمْ يَكُنْ لَكم عِنْدَهم ذَنْبٌ إلّا إيمانُكم (p-٥٧٥٩)بِاللَّهِ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وما نَقَمُوا مِنهم إلا أنْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ العَزِيزِ الحَمِيدِ﴾ [البروج: ٨] وكَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا مِن دِيارِهِمْ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إلا أنْ يَقُولُوا رَبُّنا اللَّهُ﴾ [الحج: ٤٠] وقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿إنْ كُنْتُمْ خَرَجْتُمْ﴾ أيْ: هاجَرْتُمْ ﴿جِهادًا في سَبِيلِي وابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاتِي﴾ أيْ: لِلْجِهادِ في طَرِيقِي الَّذِي شَرَعْتُهُ لَكُمْ، ودِينِي الَّذِي أمَرْتُكم بِهِ. والتِماسِ رِضائِي عَنْكُمُ الَّذِي لا ثَوابَ فَوْقَهُ، والشَّرْطُ مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِ: " لا تَتَّخِذُوا " أيْ: لا تَتَوَلَّوْا أعْدائِي إنْ كُنْتُمْ أوْلِيائِي ﴿تُسِرُّونَ إلَيْهِمْ بِالمَوَدَّةِ وأنا أعْلَمُ بِما أخْفَيْتُمْ وما أعْلَنْتُمْ﴾ أيْ: مِنَ المَوَدَّةِ مَعَهم وغَيْرِها ﴿ومَن يَفْعَلْهُ مِنكُمْ﴾ أيِ: اتِّخاذُهم أوْلِياءَ ﴿فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ﴾ أيْ: جارَ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ السَّوِيِّ الَّذِي جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ هُدًى ونَجاةً.

Meaning: You had no fault in their eyes except your belief in Allah (p-٥٧٥٩) the Lord of the worlds, as in His saying: ﴿And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Buruj: 8], and as in His saying: ﴿who were expelled from their homes without right, only because they said, "Our Lord is Allah"﴾ [al-Hajj: 40]. And His saying: ﴿If you have come out﴾, meaning: emigrated, ﴿in jihad in My cause and seeking My approval﴾, meaning: for striving in My way, which I have legislated for you, and My religion, which I have commanded you to follow, and seeking My pleasure with you, which has no reward above it. The condition is connected to "do not take", meaning: do not befriend My enemies if you are My allies. ﴿You confide to them affection, and I am most knowing of what you conceal and what you declare﴾, meaning: of the affection toward them and other than it. ﴿And whoever does it among you﴾, meaning: takes them as allies, ﴿has certainly strayed from the sound way﴾, meaning: has deviated from the straight path which Allah made a guidance and a salvation.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[2] ﴿If they gain the upper hand over you, they will be enemies to you and will extend their hands and their tongues against you with evil, and they wish that you would disbelieve.﴾

﴿If they gain the upper hand over you﴾, i.e., they prevail over you, ﴿they will be enemies to you﴾, i.e., at war with you, and casting affection toward them will not benefit you. ﴿And will extend their hands and their tongues against you with evil﴾, i.e., with that which harms you, such as killing and reviling. ﴿And they wish that you would disbelieve﴾ [an-Nisa': 89], i.e., would reject what has come to you of the truth.

The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[3] ﴿Your relatives and your children will never benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. He will decide between you, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

﴿Your relatives will never benefit you﴾ means: your kinship ties. ﴿Nor your children on the Day of Resurrection; He will decide between you﴾ means: by rewarding the believers and punishing the disobedient.

Al-Qashani said: That is, there is no benefit for those whom you chose to take as allies of the true enemy for their sake, because the Resurrection separates [people]. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿On the Day of Resurrection He will decide between you﴾, that is, Allah will separate you from your relatives and your children, as He said: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his spouse and his children﴾ [Abasa: 34–36]. End of quote. It is a good interpretation.

A subtle point:

Al-Samin said: Regarding "on the Day of Resurrection" there are two possibilities:

The first: that it relates to what precedes it, meaning: "Your relatives will never benefit you on the Day of Resurrection." Then one stops at it and begins with "He will decide between you."

The second: that it relates to what follows it, meaning: "He will decide between you on the Day of Resurrection." Then one stops at "your children" and begins with "on the Day of Resurrection."

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾, that is, He will recompense you for it.

Remarks:

The first: Ibn Jarir said: It is mentioned that these verses at the beginning of this surah were revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, who had written to the Quraysh in Makkah informing them of a matter that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had concealed from them. Then he cited the narrations.

As for the narration of al-Bukhari: "On the authority of Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me, al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad, and said: 'Go until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman carrying a letter; take it from her.' So we set off, our horses galloping with us, until we reached the garden, and there was the woman. We said: 'Bring out the letter.' She said: 'I have no letter with me!' We said: 'You will bring out the letter, or we will strip you of your clothes.' So she brought it out from her braid, and we brought it to the Prophet ﷺ, and in it was:

'From Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah to some people among the polytheists, informing them of some of the affair of the Prophet ﷺ.'

The Prophet ﷺ said: 'What is this, Hatib?' He said: 'Do not hasten against me, O Messenger of Allah! I was a man from the Quraysh, but I was not one of them by origin. Those of the Emigrants who are with you have relatives there who protect their families and property in Makkah. So I wished, since I lacked a blood tie among them, to do them a favour so that they would protect my relatives. I did not do this out of disbelief or apostasy from my religion.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'He has indeed told you the truth.' Umar said: 'Let me, O Messenger of Allah, strike his neck!' He said: 'He witnessed Badr. And what would make you know? Perhaps Allah, Mighty and Majestic, looked upon the people of Badr and said: "Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you."'"

Amr ibn Dinar, the narrator of the hadith, said: And there was revealed concerning him: ﴿O you who believe, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 1], and the verses.

Ibn Kathir said: This Hatib was a man of the Emigrants and of the people of Badr. He had property and children in Makkah, but he was not of the Quraysh by origin; rather he was an ally of Uthman. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ resolved to conquer Makkah, after its people had broken the treaty, the Prophet ﷺ commanded the Muslims to prepare for their campaign, and he said: "O Allah, conceal our news from them." Then this Hatib deliberately wrote a letter to the people of Makkah informing them of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had resolved concerning their campaign, so that he might gain a favour with them by it, as mentioned in the hadith.

The second: Ibn Kathir said: By His saying: ﴿Do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 1], Allah, Exalted, means the polytheists and the disbelievers, who are at war with Allah, His Messenger, and the believers, whose enmity and severance Allah has prescribed, and He forbade taking them as allies and friends, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another, and whoever among you allies with them is one of them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 51]. This is a severe threat and a firm warning. And Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, do not take those who have taken your religion as mockery and play from among those who were given the Scripture before you, nor the disbelievers, as allies; and fear Allah, if you are believers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 57]. And Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers. And whoever does that has nothing with Allah, except when you fear from them a danger. And Allah warns you of Himself﴾ [Al 'Imran: 28]. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted the excuse of Hatib, when he mentioned that he had only done that to placate the Quraysh, because of the property and children he had among them. End of quote.

That is, he accepted his excuse concerning what he thought was not a major sin, even though he erred. A mujtahid who errs is excused, and his error has been made clear by the explicit prohibition against repeating the like of what occasioned the revelation of this surah. For this reason the imam Ilkiya al-Harrasi said: It is derived from the verse that fear for one's property and children does not permit tumult in the religion of Allah. This is evident, and this is not taqiyyah (precautionary dissimulation), for that belongs to a different subject. The sayyid al-Murtada has expounded on loyalty and disavowal in "Iythar al-Haqq," in the eighth question. He said, after citing the verses and hadiths: All of this concerns love that is in the heart and sincere devotion for the sake of religion, and that is for the believers who are pious, by consensus, and for the monotheist Muslims, when it is for the sake of their Islam and their monotheism, according to the People of the Sunnah. As for cordiality, kindness, giving kindness, restraining anger, good manners, honouring a guest, and the like, it is recommended to extend them to all creation, except where it would entail corruption, such as humiliation; so it is not given to an enemy in a state of war, as the verse indicates: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you in religion﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 8]

[p-5763] as will come. As for taqiyyah, it is permitted for one who fears oppressive, powerful people. As for distinguishing between what is permissible of cordiality and flattery and what is impermissible of showing off, whatever concerns giving property and benefits is permissible, and this is cordiality; they sometimes call it flattery, conciliation, and good companionship. Whatever concerns matters of religion is forbidden showing off.

From the words of the imam who calls to Allah, Exalted, Yahya ibn al-Muhsin, peace be upon him, in "al-Risalah al-Mukhrasah, li-Ahl al-Madrasah": It is not permissible for loyalty to be following in matters where interpretation is possible, for many of the People of the House, peace be upon them, were known to follow the oppressors for a reason that required it. The helper [of the Imam] took many of them, and Ja'far al-Sadiq led the Friday prayer with them, and al-Hasan al-Sibt prayed over their funerals.

The imam al-Mahdi Muhammad ibn al-Mutahhar, peace be upon them both, mentioned that the prohibited loyalty by consensus is loyalty to the disbeliever for his disbelief, and to the disobedient for his disobedience, and the like.

The sayyid said: This is a sound statement. The proof for the validity of disagreement regarding what is other than that is many things, among them His saying, Exalted is He, concerning the two polytheist parents: ﴿Accompany them in this world with kindness﴾ [Luqman: 15]. Among them is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you in religion﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 8], the two verses. In a hadith it is said that it was revealed concerning Qutaylah, the mother of Asma', after the verses of prohibition. Ahmad, al-Bazzar and al-Wahidi narrated it. Its being later is clear from the context of the verses and the circumstantial evidence accompanying this hadith. Even if its being later is not established, the specific takes precedence over the general when the date is unknown, according to the majority. Ibn Rushd preferred this in his "Nihayah," on the basis of its being explicit concerning what is specific to it. It is supported by what is established in the Qur'an and the sound Sunnah, agreed upon, from the hadith of Ali, peace be upon him, in the story of Hatib, as Allah, Exalted, mentioned at the beginning of this surah, al-Mumtahanah, and as the people of hadith and the people of tafsir have all mentioned. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ excused him on account of his fear for his family in Makkah, and taqiyyah is in matters that do not harm, in his assessment.

[p-5764] If it is said: The Qur'an indicates that he had sinned, by His saying: ﴿And whoever of you does that has strayed from the right path﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 1]. How then is what came of accepting his excuse acceptable? I say: His excuse was accepted only regarding his remaining in faith and not allying with the polytheists for their polytheism. For this reason Allah addressed him with faith, saying: "O you who believe." The generality is explicit regarding its cause, so the Qur'an and the hadith agree. As for his sin, what he did is not permissible for anyone in the army except with the permission of their commander, due to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when news of security or fear reaches them, they spread it﴾ [al-Nisa': 83]. Also, the prohibition of the like of this without the commander's permission is by consensus, and with his permission it is permitted. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had permitted more than that as a stratagem for preserving property. So if the like of this were loyalty, he ﷺ would not have permitted it. This indicates that Hatib's sin was the concealment, because of the betrayal in it, not the act itself, if it were stripped of concealment and betrayal. And Allah knows best. End of quote.

To the concealment and betrayal may be added what the verse indicates of his showing affection to them by this, and offering them counsel, which reveals that the one who came with it was unsteady in his commitment and unstable in his right, so his action becomes a proof against his religion, and it becomes a cause for the polytheistic corrupters to be tempted away from the upright, true religion. This is in truth the secret, as the verse explains: ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 5]. Its explanation will come.

Then Allah, Exalted, taught His believing servants to emulate Ibrahim, peace be upon him, in disavowing the polytheists, severing ties with them, and keeping away from them, and by His saying, glorified is He:

[p-5765]

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[4] ﴿There has indeed been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from what you worship other than Allah. We have rejected you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone," except for the saying of Abraham to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you, but I have not [power to obtain] for you anything from Allah. Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned in repentance, and to You is the destination."﴾

﴿There has indeed been for you an excellent example﴾, i.e., a model, ﴿in Abraham and those with him﴾, i.e., his followers who believed with him, such as Lot, peace be upon him. ﴿When they said to their people﴾, meaning those who associated partners with Allah and worshipped the false deities, ﴿Indeed, we are disassociated [bura'a'] from you﴾ — the plural of bari', like zarif and zuraf'a. ﴿And from what you worship other than Allah. We have rejected you﴾, i.e., your religion and your objects of worship. Ibn Jarir said: i.e., we denounced what you hold of disbelief in Allah, and we denied that your worship of what you worship other than Allah is true. ﴿And there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone﴾, i.e., there is no reconciliation and no affection between us until you believe in Allah alone, that is, you affirm His oneness and single Him out in worship.

﴿Except for the saying of Abraham to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you"﴾ — this is an exception from the phrase "an excellent example." Ibn Jarir said: i.e., there has indeed been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him in these matters we have mentioned, of separating from the disbelievers and opposing them, and abandoning allegiance to them, except in the saying of Abraham to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you," for there is no example for you in that, because that was from Abraham to his father out of a promise he had made to him before it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah; when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him. He, exalted is His mention, says: Likewise, you believers in Allah, disassociate yourselves from the enemies of Allah who associate others with Him, and do not take them as allies, and show them enmity and hatred until they believe in Allah alone and disavow the worship of anything besides Him.

Then it was related from Mujahid that he said regarding the verse: they were forbidden to follow the example of Abraham's asking forgiveness for his father, so that they would not ask forgiveness for the polytheists.

﴿I have not [power to obtain] for you anything from Allah﴾, i.e., I do not avert from you anything of the punishment of Allah if He wills to punish you. The clause is part of the exception, except that it does not necessarily follow from the exception of the whole that the exception of every individual member applies. Hence al-Zamakhshari said: The intention toward the promise of asking forgiveness and what follows it is built upon it and subordinate to it, as if he said: "I will ask forgiveness for you, and I have no power except to ask forgiveness."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned in repentance, and to You is the destination﴾ is connected to what precedes the exception, and it is part of the excellent example; or it is a command from Him, exalted is He, to the believers that they should say this, completing what He enjoined upon them of severing harmful ties between them and those who fight against them. The meaning of "to You we have turned in repentance" is: to You we have returned in repentance from what You dislike, to what You love and are pleased with.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[5] ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us. Our Lord, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾

﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us. Our Lord, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ Mujahid said: that is, do not punish us at their hands, nor with a punishment from You, lest they say: "If these people were upon the truth, this would not have befallen them." Qatadah said likewise, meaning: do not let them prevail over us, lest they be tempted by that, thinking that they prevailed over us because of a truth they hold. End of quote.

The outcome of this supplication is seeking refuge from the like of what Hatib (Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah) did, which produces the temptation of the polytheists regarding the religion. For that becomes a cause for their saying: "If these people were upon the truth, and what they are promised of victory is true, their believer would not have made an arrangement with us. So what they hold is mere wishful thinking." Thus whoever had within himself an inclination to join their ranks and to seek happiness through their truth would be shaken. So in the verse there is great meaning and a mighty discipline. That is: "Our Lord, do not make us neglect any part of our religion that we have been commanded, or be lax regarding what has been decided for us from it, so that our strength does not dissolve by that, our pillar does not shake, and the enemy of the religion is not opened to temptation by it. For as long as the believers hold firmly to the etiquette of the religion, guarding it and standing by it in its true standing, victory leads them and triumph guides them. Therefore, in the later centuries the state of Muslims has become a proof against their religion before their enemy, and their word cannot be restored nor their glory regained, except by returning to the source of their Book, knowing its etiquette, guarding its rulings, and casting off what has been attached to it that distorts its word and departs from its reality. Wise people have well-known discourses on this subject."

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[6] ﴿There has certainly been for you in them an excellent pattern for whoever hopes for Allah and the Last Day. And whoever turns away - indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾

﴿There has certainly been for you in them an excellent pattern for whoever hopes for Allah and the Last Day. And whoever turns away - indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ This is a repetition, to stress the obligation of emulating (ta'assi) Abraham and his companions, and to urge further disavowal of the polytheists and avoidance of inclining towards them. For loving the corrupters entails the ruin of the foundations of truth, the weakening of its people's strength, and the casting of doubt into weak hearts, all of which corrupts the work of the sincere, shakes their efforts, and tempts their enemies through them. For this reason, hatred for the sake of Allah is one of the branches of faith (shu'ab al-iman), because truth cannot prevail except by its people's unity upon its word and by aiming at its enemies from one bow. In the substitution of ﴿for whoever hopes for Allah and the Last Day﴾ for "lakum" (for you) there is an indication that it is not befitting for a believer to abandon emulating them, and that abandoning it signals corruption of belief. For this reason he followed it with His saying:

﴿And whoever turns away - indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ That is: whoever turns away from what he has been commanded, and allies himself with the enemies of Allah, and extends affection to them, then he harms only himself, and Allah is the Free of need from his faith in Him and his obedience to Him, the Praised in every state.

(p-٥٧٦٨)

The discussion of the Exalted's saying:

[7] ﴿It may be that Allah will place affection between you and those among them with whom you have been at enmity. And Allah is Competent, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿It may be that Allah will place affection between you and those among them with whom you have been at enmity. And Allah is Competent, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ This is a promise from Him, the Exalted, and He fulfilled it, for many of them afterward embraced Islam, and they became allies and partisans for them. The verse is among the miracles of the Qur'an, because of what it contains of reporting something unseen, whose fulfillment has occurred.

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[8–9] ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion and do not expel you from your homes—from being kind to them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.﴾ ﴿Allah only forbids you from those who fight you over the religion and expel you from your homes and aid in your expulsion—[forbids you] from making allies of them. And whoever makes allies of them, it is those who are the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 9]

This is a concession from Allah, exalted is He, regarding association with those who have not opposed the believers or fought them. In meaning, it is a specification of His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 1], and so on. That is: Allah does not forbid you from those among the people of Makkah who did not fight you over the religion and did not expel you from your homes, [from] being kind to them (tabarruhum) and acting justly toward them (tuqsitu ilayhim), meaning: extending to them kindness (birr), which is goodness, and justice (qist), which is equity. This degree of friendship is not forbidden; rather, it is commanded with respect to them. Although the address is to the polytheists of Makkah, the lesson lies in the generality of its wording. Some exegetes attempted to restrict it, but Imam Ibn Jarir rejected that with his statement:

"The correct view is the view of the one who said: by His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion﴾ is meant all categories of communities and religions, [that you be] kind to them, maintain ties with them, and act justly toward them. For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, encompassed by His saying ﴿those who do not fight you over the religion and do not expel you from your homes﴾ all who have that attribute, and did not specify some of them over others. There is no sense in the statement of the one who said that this is abrogated (mansukh), because the kindness of a believer toward people of war, whether they are related to him by kinship and lineage or not, is neither prohibited nor forbidden, so long as it does not involve guiding them or the people of war to a weakness of the people of Islam, or strengthening them with horses or weapons. The report on the story of Asma' and her mother confirms the soundness of what we have said." End of quotation.

The occasion was that Asma' bint Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "My mother came to me while she was a polytheist during the period of the treaty with Quraysh. So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! My mother has come to me, desiring [my kindness]. Shall I maintain ties with her?' He said: 'Yes, maintain ties with your mother.'" Narrated by Ahmad and the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim). Ahmad also narrated it, "from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Qutaylah came to her daughter Asma' bint Abi Bakr with gifts: lizards (dabab), tanning leaves (qaraz), and ghee, while she was a polytheist. Asma' refused to accept her gift and to let her into her house, so she asked Aisha about the Prophet (ﷺ).

Then Allah revealed: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion﴾ to the end of the verse. So he commanded her to accept her gift and to let her into her house." Al-Razi said: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿that you be kind to them (tabarruhum)﴾ is a substitute (badal) for ﴿those who do not fight you﴾, and likewise ﴿that you make allies of them (tawallawhum)﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 9] is a substitute for ﴿those who fight you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 9]. The meaning: Allah does not forbid you from showing kindness to these people; He only forbids you from allying with these people. This is mercy toward them, given their severity in enmity. This verse indicates the permissibility of kindness between polytheists and Muslims, even though friendship (al-muwalah) is cut off. End of quotation.

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[8–9] ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion and do not expel you from your homes—from being kind to them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.﴾ ﴿Allah only forbids you from those who fight you over the religion and expel you from your homes and aid in your expulsion—[forbids you] from making allies of them. And whoever makes allies of them, it is those who are the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 9]

The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words, may He be exalted:

[10] ﴿O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, then test them. Allah is most knowing of their faith. And if you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for [the disbelievers], nor are [the disbelievers] lawful for them. But give the disbelievers what they have spent. And there is no blame upon you for marrying them when you have given them their bridal payments. And do not hold on to marriage bonds with disbelieving women. And ask for what you have spent and let them ask for what they have spent. That is the judgement of Allah; He judges between you. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants⦆ That is, from Makkah to Madinah. ﴿Then test them⦆ That is, examine them by what gives you a strong presumption of their truthfulness in faith. ﴿Allah is most knowing of their faith⦆ That is, the One who is aware of their hearts, not you, for that is not within your capacity; so their signs and indications suffice for you.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: When a woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would make her swear by Allah that she had not left out of hatred for a husband, and by Allah that she had not left out of desire to move from one land to another, and by Allah that she had not left in pursuit of worldly gain, and by Allah that she had not left except out of love for Allah and His Messenger.

Mujahid said: That is, ask them what brought them. If there is anger in them towards their husbands, or resentment or something else, and they have not believed, then return them to their husbands.

﴿And if you know them to be believers⦆ Al-Zamakhshari said: That is, the knowledge that your capacity reaches, namely the dominant assumption arising from the oath and the appearance of the signs. He called it knowledge only to indicate that it is like knowledge in the obligation to act upon it.

﴿Then do not return them to the disbelievers⦆ That is, do not send them back to their polytheist husbands; for there is no lawfulness between a believing woman and a polytheist, since her faith has severed her marriage bond from the polytheist who is hostile to Allah and His Messenger.

Ibn Jarir said: This was said to the believers because a treaty had taken place between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the polytheists of Quraysh at the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, that the Muslims would return to the polytheists whoever came to them as a Muslim. So that condition was nullified with regard to women who came as believing emigrants; they were tested, the Muslims found them to be believers, and this was established for them by what we have mentioned. They were commanded not to return them to the polytheists once it was known that they were believers. ﴿They are not lawful for [the disbelievers], nor are [the disbelievers] lawful for them⦆ That is, because the marriage is severed between them.

Ibn Kathir said: This verse is what made Muslim women unlawful for polytheist men. At the beginning of Islam it had been permissible for a polytheist to marry a believing woman. For this reason, the matter of Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi', husband of the daughter of the Prophet ﷺ, Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with her, was as follows: she was a Muslim while he was upon the religion of his people. When the captives fell at the Battle of Badr, his wife Zaynab sent, for his ransom, a necklace that had belonged to her mother Khadijah. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw it, he was greatly moved with tenderness towards her, and he said to the Muslims: "If you see fit to release her captive for her, then do so." So they did, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ released him on condition that he send his daughter to him. He fulfilled that, and was truthful in what he promised, and sent her to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with Zayd ibn Harithah, may Allah be pleased with him. She remained in Madinah from after the Battle of Badr, and that was in the second year, until her husband Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi' embraced Islam in the eighth year, and he returned her to him under the first marriage contract, without giving her a new dowry. Some say it was after two years, and that is correct, for his conversion was two years after the prohibition of Muslim women to polytheists. End of quote.

﴿But give them what they have spent⦆ Ibn Jarir said: That is, give the polytheists whose wives have come to you as believers, when you know them to be believers, and you did not return them to them, what they had spent on their marriage to them of the bridal payment. ﴿And there is no blame upon you for marrying them⦆ That is, these emigrant women who have joined you from the abode of war, separated from their husbands, even if they had husbands. ﴿When you have given them their bridal payments⦆ That is, their dowries. Ibn Zayd said: Because Islam separated them once their wombs had been cleared.

Then he indicated that, just as the marriage of a believing woman to a disbeliever is void, so too the marriage of a disbelieving woman to a Muslim is void, by His saying: ﴿And do not hold on to marriage bonds with disbelieving women⦆ That is, to their contracts by which one holds on to make lawful.

Ibn Jarir said: He, whose praise is exalted, says to the believers in Him among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Do not, O believers, hold on to the ties and bonds of disbelieving women. "Kawafir" is the plural of "kafirah". "Isam" is the plural of "ismah", which is what one holds on to of a contract or a tie. This is a prohibition from Allah, exalted, to the believers against proceeding to marry polytheist women from the people of idols, and a command to them to separate from them. Then it is narrated from Mujahid, who said: The companions of Muhammad were commanded to divorce their disbelieving wives in Makkah who had remained with the disbelievers.

And from al-Zuhri: When this verse was revealed, ﴿O you who have believed⦆ up to His saying ﴿And do not hold on to marriage bonds with disbelieving women⦆, among those who divorced were Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, two wives he had in Makkah: the daughter of Abu Umayyah and the daughter of Jarwal. And Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah [divorced] the daughter of Rabi'ah; so Islam separated them when the Qur'an forbade holding on to the marriage bonds of disbelieving women. Among those who had fled to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the women of the disbelievers, who had no treaty between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he detained them and married them to Muslim men. Umaymah daughter of Bishr al-Ansariyyah had been married to Thabit ibn al-Dahdahah; she fled from him, while he was then a disbeliever, to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married her to Sahl ibn Hunayf, of the clan of Banu Amr ibn Awf, and she bore Abd Allah ibn Sahl.

﴿And ask for what you have spent⦆ That is: O believers, seek back from the polytheists whose wives have fled and joined the polytheists what you spent on your wives who have joined them, of the bridal payment, for those of them who have married. ﴿And let them ask for what they have spent⦆ That is: and let the polytheists ask you for what they spent on those believing women who joined you, if they marry among you, from whoever among you married them, what they spent on them of the bridal payment. ﴿That is the judgement of Allah; He judges between you, and Allah is Knowing and Wise⦆ That is: this ruling, which was decided by the Commander of the Believers in asking the polytheists for what they had spent, and commanded the polytheists to do the same, is the judgement of Allah, the Truth, from which none turns away.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[11] ﴿And if any of your wives escape you to the disbelievers, and then you have a turn (of victory), then give to those whose wives have gone the like of what they had spent. And fear Allah, in whom you are believers.﴾

﴿And if any of your wives escape you to the disbelievers﴾ meaning: and if a woman from among you apostatizes and joins the disbelievers, and they do not return her dowry, ﴿and then you have a turn﴾ meaning: you fight them and acquire spoils from them, ﴿then give to those whose wives have gone﴾ meaning: from among the Muslims, ﴿the like of what they had spent﴾ meaning: as their dowries.

Mujahid said: the equivalent of her dowry is paid to her husband.

Qatadah said: When they fled from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ to the disbelievers, with no treaty between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ then obtained spoils, the husband of the woman was given from the whole of the spoils an amount equal to what he had paid her as dowry, and then they divided up their spoils.

(p-5774) ﴿And fear Allah, in whom you are believers﴾ meaning: for belief in Him requires carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

The commentary on His words, Exalted is He:

[12] ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children, nor bring a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet, nor disobey you in what is right, then accept their pledge and ask Allah's forgiveness for them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal﴾. Ibn Kathir said: That is, the wealth of other people. As for when the husband is unable to maintain her, she may take from his property what is customary for women like her, even without his knowledge, acting upon the hadith of Hind bint Utbah, that she said: "O Messenger of Allah! Abu Sufyan is a stingy man. He does not give me enough maintenance to suffice me and my son. Is it a sin upon me if I take from his property without his knowledge?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Take from his property what is customary, what suffices you and your sons." It was narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim in their two Sahihs.

﴿nor commit adultery, nor kill their children﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: It means burying daughters alive.

Ibn Kathir said: This includes killing a child after its existence, as the people of the Jahiliyyah used to kill their children for fear of poverty, and it also includes killing it while it is still a fetus, as some ignorant women may do, by harming themselves so that they do not conceive, whether for a corrupt purpose or something similar.

(p-5775) ﴿nor bring a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet﴾. Ibn Abbas said: That is, they should not attribute to their husbands children who are not theirs. Al-Zamakhshari clarified it with his words: A woman would pick up a newborn and say to her husband, "This is my child from you." The phrase "a slander invented between their hands and their feet" is a euphemism for the child that she attributes falsely to her husband, because the belly in which she carries it lies between the hands, and the womb from which she gives birth lies between the feet. So it is other than adultery, and there is no repetition in it.

Al-Shihab said, in al-Kirmani's Sharh al-Bukhari, its meaning is: Do not bring a slander from yourselves. The hand and the foot are a metaphor for the self, because most actions are done by them, and for this reason it is said to one who is punished for a verbal offence: "This is what your two hands have earned." Or its meaning is: Do not produce it from your consciences and hearts, because it comes from the heart, whose seat is between the hands and the feet. The first is a metaphor for fabricating slander on their own initiative, and the second for it arising from the innermost core of their hearts, which reflects inner corruption.

Al-Khattabi said: Its meaning is: Do not slander people face to face and in confrontation, as one says to a person present before you, "He is before you." It is refuted by saying that although they used an expression of the present by saying it is "between his hands," one does not say "between his feet," and it would be valid if the feet alone were mentioned; but with the hands mentioned as a consequence, it is not. So the one who errs is in error. It is a metaphor for tearing the veil of modesty. What is meant is the prohibition of slander, and it includes lying and backbiting. End of quote.

﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾. That is, in the commandments of Allah that you order them to follow.

In al-Nihayah it is said: Al-ma'ruf (what is known and good) is a comprehensive term for everything known as obedience to Allah, kindness to people, and everything the Sharia has commanded and forbidden.

﴿then accept their pledge and ask Allah's forgiveness for them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. That is: accept their pledge to fulfil these matters, and ask Allah to forgive their sins and pardon them, for He is Forgiving and Merciful to whoever repents of them.

Notes:

First: al-Bukhari narrated from Aisha that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to test the believing women who emigrated to him with this verse. Whoever among the believing women affirmed this condition, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say to her: "I have accepted your pledge," in words only. By Allah, his hand never touched the hand of any woman in the pledge; he accepted their pledge only with his words: "I have accepted your pledge regarding that."

Ibn Hajar said: That is, there was no handshake, as was the customary practice of shaking hands with men at the time of the pledge.

Then he said: al-Nasa'i and al-Tabari narrated that Umayma bint Ruqayqah informed him that she entered among a group of women who were pledging allegiance. They said: "O Messenger of Allah! Extend your hand that we may shake it." He said: "I do not shake hands with women, but I will take your pledge." He took the pledge from us until he reached "nor disobey you in what is right," and he said: "In what you are able and capable of." They said: "Allah and His Messenger are more merciful to us than we are to ourselves." In a narration of al-Tabari: "My saying to one hundred women is no different from my saying to one woman." Other reports have also come that they used to take his hand at the pledge over a garment. This was recorded by Yahya ibn Sallam in his Tafsir from al-Sha'bi.

In Ibn Ishaq's al-Maghazi, from Aban ibn Salih, that he would dip his hand into a vessel, and the women would dip their hands into it. End of quote.

What is relied upon is al-Bukhari's first narration because it is sound, and the weakness of the others.

Second: Muslim narrated from Umm Atiyyah, who said: When this verse was revealed, "nor disobey you in what is right," it included wailing (al-niyahah) over the dead.

The wording of al-Bukhari from her is: "We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He recited to us: ﴿that they will not associate anything with Allah﴾, and he forbade us from wailing."

al-Tabari, with his chain, narrated from a woman among those who pledged: "Among what was taken from us was that we would not disobey him in anything that is right, nor scratch our faces, nor loosen our hair, nor tear our collars, nor call out 'woe'."

From Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) took the pledge from them that day that they would not wail, and that they would not speak to men except a man of their own who was a mahram. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said: "O Prophet of Allah! We have guests, and we are away from our women?" He said: "It is not those I meant."

Third: al-Kiya al-Harrasi said: It is derived from His words, Exalted is He: ﴿nor disobey you in what is right﴾, that there is no obedience to anyone in what is not right. He said: The command of the Prophet (ﷺ) was only ever in what is right, and his condition regarding obedience was only so that no one would grant a dispensation for obedience to rulers.

Its origin is what al-Tabari narrated from Ibn Zayd, who said regarding this verse: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was His prophet and the chosen one among His creation, yet no command was made lawful for him except with a condition. He did not say: ﴿and they will not disobey you﴾ and leave it there, until He said: ﴿in what is right﴾. So how should it be befitting for anyone to be obeyed in what is not right, when Allah has made this a condition for His Prophet?

Then, at the end of the surah, He, Exalted is He, drew attention to what He had drawn attention to at its beginning, namely the prohibition of allying with the enemies of the religion, as a warning against negligence in this matter and as an increase in care for it. So He, Glorified is He, said:

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[13] ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as allies a people with whom Allah has been angry, who have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, do not take as allies a people with whom Allah has been angry﴾ That is: upon whom His wrath has descended, because of their hostility to the truth, their warring against righteousness, and their spreading of corruption. It is general to every warrior, though some have restricted it to the Jews, since He described them elsewhere as "those who have earned anger" (al-maghdub 'alayhim). Al-Zamakhshari confined himself to this view. Al-Nasir said: Al-Zamakhshari had mentioned, in his commentary on His saying, ﴿And the two seas are not alike﴾ [Fatir: 12] up to His saying ﴿and from each you eat fresh meat﴾ [Fatir: 12], that the end of the verse is an digression (istitrad), which is one of the arts of eloquent expression, classified under it by its specialists. This verse of al-Mumtahanah may very well be of this art, for it censures the Jews and, by way of digression, extends the censure to the polytheists, in a fine manner of association. The eloquent cannot find anything better or more fitting for digression than this. Among the verses with which they introduced this art is his saying:

Whenever a young man fears Allah and obeys Him, there is no fault in him, even if he were of a criminal lineage.

And his saying:

If you were lying in what you told me, then you escaped as al-Harith ibn Hisham escaped.

And his saying:

He left his beloveds to fend for themselves, and escaped on the head of a swift horse and its bridle.

End of quotation.

(p-5779) The reason he preferred fleeing from emphasis (ta'kid) to foundation (ta'sis), while the meaning intended by the beginning of the surah is included in it, is that it contains the rhetorical embellishment of returning the final part to the first part (radd al-ajuz 'ala al-sadr), serving as a reminder and a magnification, for the sake of giving attention to its matter. Each has its own direction.

﴿they have despaired of the Hereafter﴾ That is: of its reward, because of their denial of it, and for this reason they transgressed, rebelled, and spread corruption. The clause is a second description. ﴿just as the disbelievers have despaired of those in the graves﴾ That is: just as those disbelievers before them, their fellow unbelievers who are buried, have despaired, meaning: they are of the same kind as those before them, and each is held accountable for his disbelief. It has also been said: the meaning is as the disbelievers have despaired that the people of the graves, who have died, will return to them. In this there is the placing of the apparent noun in the position of the pronoun, to record their disbelief and to clarify what required the anger upon them and what made them despair. The first is more apparent.
